public_rationale: Supported under the ordinary reading that hallucinations can arise from how language models learn and generate, without a software defect. Technical work public before the post establishes such causes. The architectural wording is imprecise: the strongest cited result explicitly applies independently of transformer architecture and allows mitigation. It does not support a stronger claim that hallucinations cannot be reduced or avoided on particular tasks.
limitations: The result depends on reading feature as a structural tendency of the model system, not a transformer-specific defect.
The mathematical results have restricted assumptions and do not measure practical error rates.
The claim that nobody is making progress is outside this assessment.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Hallucinations are not a bug so much as a feature of the transformer model that underpins generative AI.

statement.excerpt: Hallucinations are not a bug, so much as a feature of the transformer model that underpins generative AI.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that hallucinations can arise from the normal learning and generation process of transformer language models, rather than requiring an implementation defect.
Feature is understood as a structural tendency, not an intended product capability.
The sentence does not explicitly say that transformers uniquely hallucinate, that every response must hallucinate, or that mitigation is impossible.
The adjacent assertion that nobody is closer to solving hallucinations is a separate claim and is not graded here.
criteria.support_condition: Technical analysis or controlled experiments demonstrate hallucinations arising under correct model operation from learning, prediction or information limits applicable to transformer language models.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence establishes that the relevant hallucinations require implementation defects and disappear when those defects are corrected without changing the learning or generation problem.

evidence.explanation: The analysis establishes a statistical source of hallucination for calibrated predictors of certain arbitrary facts, even with ideal factual training data. The result is independent of transformer architecture and permits mitigation, so it supports the ordinary structural-tendency reading rather than architectural inevitability.

The paper derives limitations from the inability to learn every computable ground-truth function, without assuming an implementation defect. Its broad formal definition does not establish an unavoidable error rate for any particular practical task.
